title: {{NAME}} and the Ancient Emergency
moral: Old wisdom and new power are most effective when they work together.
character_anchor: Bright children's book cartoon illustration, bold outlines, vivid flat colours. {{NAME}}, a young boy with brown hair and blue eyes, wearing a forest-green hero suit with amber-gold lightning trim, dark boots, and amber gloves — same child, same face, same exact outfit in every image.

pages.content:
The temporal fault opened in the city centre on a Tuesday at noon.

Through it: three confused Stegosauruses and a Stegosaurus who was already unhappy about something unrelated.

The city's heroes had the area evacuated in twelve minutes.

The problem now: getting four prehistoric dinosaurs back through a fault that was shrinking.

The Fairy Historical Council arrived simultaneously. They had been monitoring the fault for two weeks.

"We tried to tell someone," said the head fairy to {{NAME}}.

"I'm told now," said {{NAME}}. "What do you know about the Stegosaurus's mood?"

pages.content:
The fairies knew: the Stegosaurus was territorial and stressed by the unfamiliar environment, and would charge if it felt cornered.

{{NAME}}'s power: electromagnetic fields, useful for large obstacles but possibly catastrophic near distressed prehistoric animals.

"Don't use the field," said the head fairy.

"I know," said {{NAME}}.

"Most heroes don't know," she said.

"Most heroes don't consult the Fairy Historical Council," he said. "What does it respond well to?"

"Open space. Familiar sounds. The smell of its era's vegetation."

{{NAME}} thought for thirty seconds. Then he called the botanical garden.

pages.content:
The botanical garden had Cretaceous-era plant species in its prehistoric wing.

With permission, {{NAME}} borrowed a cart of them: ancient ferns, cycads, ginkgo branches.

He wheeled them toward the Stegosaurus himself, slowly, leaving a trail of scent.

The dinosaur stopped pacing. Lifted its head. Followed.

The fairies simultaneously calmed the three Stegosauruses with light and sound frequencies from that era.

All four dinosaurs were within ten metres of the fault in forty minutes.

pages.content:
The Stegosauruses went through calmly.

The Stegosaurus stopped at the fault edge. Turned. Looked at {{NAME}} from three metres away.

{{NAME}} stood very still.

The Stegosaurus made a sound like two rocks colliding, but quieter. Almost conversational.

Then it walked through.

The fault closed.

The city was silent.

The head fairy landed on {{NAME}}'s shoulder. "You didn't use the field."

"I didn't need to," he said. "It just needed the right information."

pages.content:
He walked home through the city's empty-then-returning streets.

The carts of prehistoric plants had been returned. The fairies had dispersed. The heroes were writing their reports.

{{NAME}} was thinking about the Stegosaurus's sound at the fault edge.

Almost conversational. Something to say before leaving.

In bed, he lay in the dark wondering what it had meant.

He fell asleep before he worked it out, and dreamed in Cretaceous green.
